units.text: INT. SALT MINE CHAPEL - NIGHT
A cathedral carved from rock salt, a thousand feet below the earth.
Chandeliers of crystal hang from a vaulted ceiling.
The walls glow faint pink in the lamplight.
Pews of carved salt face an altar whose carved relief shows the Last Supper, every face worn smooth by humidity.
DETECTIVE AMARA OSEI-LINDQVIST (40s, hard hat over a bun, heavy coat, notebook sealed in a plastic bag) stands at the altar rail, holding a flashlight.
Her breath hangs in the cold.
FATHER BENEDIKT WRÓBLEWSKI (60s, black cassock, miner's lamp strapped to his forehead, a rosary wound around one gnarled hand) kneels at the altar's foot, staring at the floor.
Between them, on the salt floor, a dark stain.
Father, I need you to look at me.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: I have been looking at it for six hours.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Then look at me.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: He lifts his head slowly.
His eyes are clear and wet.
When did you last see Brother Tomasz?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: At Vespers.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Alone?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: No.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Who was with him?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Benedikt does not answer.
He turns the rosary beads, one at a time.
Somewhere in the dark, a pump coughs.
Father.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: God forgive me.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Not yet. First, tell me what you saw.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: I saw nothing! I saw nothing at all!
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: His voice echoes off the carved walls.
Salt sifts from the ceiling like snow.
Amara waits until it settles.
There are only two ways into this chapel. The lift, and the old shaft. I've checked both.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Then you know.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: I know the lift has been locked since midnight.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: And the shaft?
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Someone used it. Recently. There are fresh boot marks in the brine.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Benedikt closes his eyes.
Cassock hem was wet when I came in.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: What?
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Nothing.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: She steps around the stain, studying the angle of the carved altar.
The flashlight beam finds a smear of red on the base of the relief, a small, deliberate handprint at about shoulder height.
That's not blood.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: It is paint.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Why would there be paint on the altar?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Brother Tomasz was restoring the faces.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Which ones?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: The apostles.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: She raises the light.
Twelve faces, worn blank.
One of them, third from the left, has been freshly carved: gaunt, kind, familiar.
Benedikt looks up.
His mouth opens, closes.
Father. That face is yours.
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Yes.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Why would he carve you into the altar?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Because I asked him to.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: Why?
units.name: AMARA

units.text: Because I wanted to be remembered.
units.name: BENEDIKT

units.text: The pump coughs again.
Amara lowers the flashlight.
The chapel plunges into gentle pink dark, and the two figures stand in it, listening to the salt settle.
